seoDescription: Enhance your Ionic application's startup experience by moving beyond static splash screens. This guide demonstrates how to create and implement custom animated splash screens for a more professional and engaging user feel. Learn the fundamentals of generating standard splash assets using Cordova resources, then dive into advanced techniques. Discover how to use inline SVG files with CSS animations for lightweight, custom transitions. Additionally, explore how to integrate complex Lottie animations using a dedicated Cordova plugin.

chapters.title: Generating a Basic Ionic Splash Screen
chapters.description: Learn how to use the 'ionic cordova resources' command to automatically generate standard splash screens and icons for your app.

chapters.title: Configuring the Native Splash Screen
chapters.description: Explore the configuration options available in config.xml and the Ionic Native plugin for controlling the splash screen's behavior.

chapters.title: Basic Splash Screen Demo
chapters.description: See the default generated splash screen in action on an iOS simulator and learn how to hide the loading spinner.

chapters.title: Setting Up an Animated SVG Splash Screen
chapters.description: This chapter covers the first method for an animated splash screen: using an inline SVG file within the app's root component.

chapters.title: Implementing SVG Animation Logic & CSS
chapters.description: Write the TypeScript and CSS code to control the SVG animation, hiding it and revealing the main app content after a set duration.

chapters.title: Demo of the Animated SVG
chapters.description: Watch the custom SVG animation play during app startup before transitioning to the main user interface.

chapters.title: Introducing Lottie Splash Screens
chapters.description: Learn about Lottie, a library for rich animations, and how to set up the Cordova plugin for using Lottie animations as a splash screen.

chapters.title: Configuring the Lottie Splash Screen
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to configure the Lottie plugin in config.xml and use its Ionic Native wrapper to control the animation.

chapters.title: Demoing the Lottie Splash Screen
chapters.description: See the final result of integrating a Lottie animation as the app's splash screen, running on the iOS simulator.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Final Thoughts
chapters.description: The video concludes with a summary of the different splash screen techniques and a call to action for further learning.

summary:
## Generating a Standard Splash Screen

The most basic way to add a splash screen to an Ionic app is using the built-in Cordova tooling.
- **Command**: `ionic cordova resources`
- **Required Files**: Your project needs a `resources/icon.png` (at least 1024x1024) and `resources/splash.png` (at least 2732x2732). The command uses these source files to generate all necessary sizes for iOS and Android.

## Configuring the Native Splash Screen

You can control the behavior of the default splash screen in `config.xml`.
- **Key Preferences**:
    - `<preference name="SplashScreenDelay" value="3000" />`: How long the splash screen stays visible.
    - `<preference name="FadeSplashScreenDuration" value="300" />`: Duration of the fade-out effect.
    - `<preference name="ShowSplashScreenSpinner" value="false" />`: Hides the default native loading spinner.
- **Programmatic Control**: The Cordova `SplashScreen` plugin (included by default) allows you to hide the splash screen from your code, typically in `app.component.ts` once the platform is ready: `this.splashScreen.hide();`

## Method 1: Animated SVG Splash Screen

This is a lightweight approach for simple, custom animations using CSS.

- **Core Logic**:
    1. Place your SVG markup directly inside `app.component.html`.
    2. Use an `*ngIf="!routerHidden"` on your SVG container and `*ngIf="routerHidden"` on `<ion-router-outlet>` to toggle visibility.
    3. In your component's CSS file, define keyframe animations for the elements inside your SVG (e.g., targeting them by ID).
    4. In `app.component.ts`, use a `setTimeout` that matches your CSS animation's duration. After the timeout, set `routerHidden = true` and also set the SVG container's display style to `none` to ensure it's removed from view.

## Method 2: Animated Lottie Splash Screen

Use the `cordova-plugin-lottie-splashscreen` for rich, complex animations created in Adobe After Effects.

- **Setup**:
    1. Install the Cordova plugin and its `@ionic-native/lottie-splash-screen` wrapper.
    2. Add `LottieSplashScreen` to the `providers` array in your `app.module.ts`.
    3. Place your Lottie animation file (e.g., `animation.json`) inside the `src/assets` folder.
- **Configuration in `config.xml`**:
    - First, disable the default splash screen: `<preference name="SplashScreen" value="none" />`
    - Add Lottie-specific preferences:
        - `<preference name="LottieSplashScreenLocation" value="www/assets/lottie.json" />`
        - `<preference name="LottieFullScreen" value="true" />`
        - `<preference name="LottieBackgroundColor" value="#ffffff" />`
 
> [!TIP]
> The Lottie plugin allows you to loop an animation until your app's initial data is loaded. You can then programmatically hide it by injecting `LottieSplashScreen` and calling `this.lottieSplashScreen.hide();`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> When implementing a custom splash screen, you might encounter caching issues on iOS where the old native splash screen continues to appear. A full app reinstall on the device or simulator can often resolve this.

Here we go with a splash screen generated in all the different sizes for all the different applications and once you now run `ionic cordova build whatever iOS and Android`, these files will be copied over to your native application. So that is the basic of having a splash screen or also an icon.

## Configuring the Native Splash Screen

This splash screen is not just an image, and you can find how it actually is displayed and how long inside your config.xml. And of course the icons as well, using Cordova resources. Applying an SVG is a simple way to animate the splash screen with a few elements that you might change with the CSS animation, or if you're fancy, use Lottie animations instead of the general Cordova splash screen.
